name: Haiyue Zhu

papers.title: AWLS: Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering for One-Step Generative Robotic Manipulation Policies
papers.abstract: Human-collected real-world robotic manipulation demonstrations often contain mixed-quality trajectories, including hesitant, indirect, or inefficient action segments. While diffusion- and flow-based policies can model such multimodal data, standard behavior cloning (BC) assigns equal likelihood to all demonstrated actions and may therefore reproduce suboptimal modes. Offline RL value estimates offer a natural signal for biasing policies toward higher-value behavioral modes, but directly fine-tuning the generative policy or using critic gradients for policy steering can amplify critic errors and induce prior drift. We propose Advantage-Weighted Latent Steering (AWLS), an offline post-training method for improving frozen one-step generative manipulation policies without updating their decoders. AWLS learns a residual noise shaper, an observation-conditioned residual correction to the policy's latent noise, and trains it with an advantage-weighted action reconstruction objective. The advantages are detached, scale-normalized, and used only as supervised weights on demonstrated actions, avoiding critic-gradient policy updates while preserving fast single-step inference. We further introduce a rollout-free decoder-sensitivity criterion for selecting pretrained checkpoints that remain responsive to latent-noise perturbations. Experiments on simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks with clean and mixed-quality demonstrations show that AWLS improves over the frozen base policy while limiting drift from the pretrained behavior prior.

papers.title: FR-VLA: Implicit Force Reasoning VLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Integrating Vision-Language-Action Model (VLA) with force awareness is not merely a matter of encoding wrench measurements as an additional modality, but of determining the optimal timing and strength when and how physical interaction should influence contact-conditioned robot action generation. Existing force-aware VLAs typically treat force-to-action conditioning as a constant channel, leaving its decision relevance to be inferred implicitly during action prediction. We argue that force-informed action generation requires an intermediate force-relevance mechanism inside the VLA, where visual-language context estimates the task-dependent relevance of physical feedback before force is injected into the action pathway. FR-VLA addresses this gap with a VLM-based implicit force reasoning module that derives a vision-language-grounded force-admission signal from learnable force-query tokens and uses it to modulate an external tokenized force pathway for action generation. Real-world experiments on two robotic platforms and five contact-rich tasks show a 20.8% average success rate improvement over the strongest baseline, with visualizations confirming phase-dependent force admission dynamics.

papers.title: Noise-Invariant Spatial Encoding for 3D Manipulation Policies under Depth Corruption
papers.abstract: 3D manipulation policies derive actions from explicit scene geometry rather than color images alone, enabling them to reason over metric distances, object relations, and robot-scene reachability. This geometric interface is also a vulnerability: commodity RGB-D sensors return missing measurements, boundary artifacts, and plausible but wrong surfaces around transparent, reflective, thin, or textureless objects. We study this failure under realistic depth corruption and observe a sharp depth-noise cliff across modern 3D policies, even when they are trained with matched noisy depth. This residual gap motivates a spatial-encoding approach: corrupted depth becomes entangled with the token coordinates and geometry features consumed by the action expert. We propose Noise-Invariant Spatial Encoding (NISE), a 3D policy architecture that learns trustworthy geometry features even facing imperfect depth. NISE uses Geometric Cross-View Self-Supervision to shape shared policy features with calibrated multi-view depth, and Gaussian Marginalized 3D Attention to carry position uncertainty into deployed attention rather than treating every lifted token as exact. Across simulated benchmarks with sensor-realistic corruption and real-robot tasks involving transparent and reflective materials, NISE improves depth-noise robustness while preserving clean-depth performance, supporting 3D policies designed for commodity RGB-D deployment rather than clean-depth benchmarks alone.
institutions: Singapore Institute of Manufacturing Technology, A*STAR

papers.title: Physics-Guided Biomechanical Gait Adaptation for Humanoid Locomotion on Extreme Sloped Terrains
papers.abstract:
Model-free reinforcement learning has enabled impressive humanoid locomotion. Existing methods are dedicated to developing policies that can locomote on complex terrains, but locomotion on sloped terrain is seldom explored, requiring simultaneous stability and posture control.
To address these challenges, we propose a two-stage framework with physics guidance for blind humanoid slope locomotion. In Stage I, we learn a general locomotion prior with a terrain-aligned apparent Zero Moment Point (ZMP) regularizer, evaluating balance on a local support plane rather than a world-horizontal plane. However, the trained policies on steep inclines often present inefficient crouched gaits and unnatural postures that overuse the low Center of Mass (CoM) for short-term stability.
To handle these issues, we further introduce the Biomechanical Slope Gait Adapter (BSGA) in Stage II, which uses PCA-extracted macroscopic terrain descriptors as training-only critic inputs and reward-gating signals. It conditions CoM-height, joint-level gait, and swing-leg priors on the estimated slope geometry, encouraging hip-dominant uphill propulsion and knee-oriented downhill braking while keeping the deployed actor purely proprioceptive. To address the absence of simulators, we also develop a variety of uphill terrain environments for policy training based on Isaac Lab.
Sim-to-real experiments on a real-world Unitree G1 show that our method mitigates crouched-gait degeneration and enables blind continuous traversal of outdoor grass slopes up to 25°, providing a physics-informed approach for robust humanoid locomotion on steep inclines.

keywords: Humanoid Locomotion, Sloped Terrains, Reinforcement Learning
